North Carolina Federal Bankruptcy Data

North Carolina pro se debtors face the same federal rules as represented filers but without a licensed advocate. Dismissal rates tend to run higher for pro se cases, often for procedural reasons (missed deadlines, incomplete schedules) rather than merits.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 827 consumer bankruptcy cases from North Carolina's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7273n/an/a

Chapter 13554n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Pro Se Works in North Carolina

The profile of a North Carolina pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the North Carolina median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in North Carolina

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The North Carolina exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

North Carolina Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the North Carolina exemption scheme:

North Carolina homestead: $35,000 ($70,000 joint / $60,000 60+) (NCGS 1C-1601(a)(1)).

North Carolina auto exemption: $3,500 ($1,500 per debtor + joint).

North Carolina wage protection: BANNED for consumer debts.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

## Pro Se Bankruptcy in North Dakota [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/states/north-dakota.html

← prosebankruptcy.org home

Pro Se Bankruptcy in North Dakota [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for North Dakota residents.

Yes, you can file bankruptcy without a lawyer (pro se) in North Dakota. The federal bankruptcy courts in North Dakota accept pro se filings, and the official forms are free at uscourts.gov. Pro se works best for a straightforward Chapter 7 with few assets and no disputes; it gets risky if you have property to protect, a business, income near the means-test limit, or any contested issue. Check North Dakota's local rules and the court's self-help resources before filing, and confirm your exemptions, because mistakes on a pro se petition are hard to undo.

Pro Se Bankruptcy in North Dakota - Overview

Individuals have the constitutional right to represent themselves under 28 U.S.C. Section 1654. Corporations and LLCs cannot file pro se - Rowland v. California Men's Colony, 506 U.S. 194 (1993). For individual Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 filers in North Dakota, pro se is legally permitted but practically difficult.

North Dakota Pro Se FactsValue

Chapter 7 pro se rate (FJC)n/a

Chapter 13 pro se rate (FJC)n/a

Bankruptcy districtsDistrict of North Dakota

Local pro se ruleD.N.D. low volume; pro se accepted.

North Dakota Self-Help Resources

Legal Services of ND.

Additional North Dakota resources for pro se bankruptcy filers:

LawHelp.org ND - triage tool linking to free/low-cost legal aid.

State bar lawyer referral service - 30-minute consultations often at reduced fee.

Court-run pro se clinics - many North Dakota bankruptcy judges host periodic free clinics; check the district's website.

Law school bankruptcy clinics - where available (see above), these accept clinic-eligible clients.

U.S. Trustee Program - the UST does not represent debtors but will point out procedural problems; in Bankruptcy Administrator states (NC and SC) the Administrator handles this role.

North Dakota Local Rule Pitfalls for Pro Se Filers

D.N.D. low volume; pro se accepted.

Beyond the federal Bankruptcy Code and Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, each North Dakota bankruptcy district has its own Local Rules and Standing Orders that are NOT negotiable. Common pro se traps:

Local form requirements. North Dakota districts often have local cover sheets, pay-advice summaries, or tax-return cover forms that supplement the national Official Forms.

E-filing restrictions. Pro se filers generally cannot use CM/ECF unless they register and complete training. Paper filing is the default.

Paper originals for signatures. Many North Dakota districts require wet-signed originals for petitions, schedules, and amendments.

Credit counseling certificate timing. The certificate must be dated before filing (no grace period except very narrow hardship exceptions).

341 meeting attendance requirements. In-person attendance rules vary by district; some North Dakota courts require video, some allow telephone.

Redaction requirements under Rule 9037. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 9037 mandates SSN, account number, and minor-child redactions. Pro se filers are fully responsible for compliance.

See common pro se mistakes.

UPL (Unauthorized Practice of Law) in North Dakota

N.D.C.C. 27-11-01 UPL.

For pro se debtors, UPL has two practical faces:

Protection: Non-lawyers (friends, family, internet forum commenters) cannot give you legal advice in North Dakota. If they do, their advice is unreliable and they may be prosecuted.

Limit on help: The only non-lawyer assistance permitted in bankruptcy is from Bankruptcy Petition Preparers (BPPs) under 11 U.S.C. Section 110. BPPs may type the forms you tell them to type but may not advise on law. They must disclose their identity and fees.

A BPP who crosses the line into legal advice commits UPL and can be sanctioned; the debtor may be allowed to recover fees paid. See 11 U.S.C. Section 110.

When Pro Se Works in North Dakota

The profile of a North Dakota pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the North Dakota median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in North Dakota

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The North Dakota exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

North Dakota Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the North Dakota exemption scheme:

North Dakota homestead: $100,000 (N.D.C.C. 47-18-01).

North Dakota auto exemption: $1,200 (or $32,000 disabled).

North Dakota wage protection: 25%.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

Court-run pro se clinics - many Pennsylvania bankruptcy judges host periodic free clinics; check the district's website.

Law school bankruptcy clinics - where available (see above), these accept clinic-eligible clients.

U.S. Trustee Program - the UST does not represent debtors but will point out procedural problems; in Bankruptcy Administrator states (NC and SC) the Administrator handles this role.

Pennsylvania Local Rule Pitfalls for Pro Se Filers

PAEB/PAWB/PAMB have pro se intake; Philadelphia and Pittsburgh high volume.

Beyond the federal Bankruptcy Code and Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, each Pennsylvania bankruptcy district has its own Local Rules and Standing Orders that are NOT negotiable. Common pro se traps:

Local form requirements. Pennsylvania districts often have local cover sheets, pay-advice summaries, or tax-return cover forms that supplement the national Official Forms.

E-filing restrictions. Pro se filers generally cannot use CM/ECF unless they register and complete training. Paper filing is the default.

Paper originals for signatures. Many Pennsylvania districts require wet-signed originals for petitions, schedules, and amendments.

Credit counseling certificate timing. The certificate must be dated before filing (no grace period except very narrow hardship exceptions).

341 meeting attendance requirements. In-person attendance rules vary by district; some Pennsylvania courts require video, some allow telephone.

Redaction requirements under Rule 9037. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 9037 mandates SSN, account number, and minor-child redactions. Pro se filers are fully responsible for compliance.

See common pro se mistakes.

UPL (Unauthorized Practice of Law) in Pennsylvania

42 Pa.C.S. 2524 UPL.

For pro se debtors, UPL has two practical faces:

Protection: Non-lawyers (friends, family, internet forum commenters) cannot give you legal advice in Pennsylvania. If they do, their advice is unreliable and they may be prosecuted.

Limit on help: The only non-lawyer assistance permitted in bankruptcy is from Bankruptcy Petition Preparers (BPPs) under 11 U.S.C. Section 110. BPPs may type the forms you tell them to type but may not advise on law. They must disclose their identity and fees.

A BPP who crosses the line into legal advice commits UPL and can be sanctioned; the debtor may be allowed to recover fees paid. See 11 U.S.C. Section 110.

Pennsylvania Federal Bankruptcy Data

Pennsylvania pro se debtors face the same federal rules as represented filers but without a licensed advocate. Dismissal rates tend to run higher for pro se cases, often for procedural reasons (missed deadlines, incomplete schedules) rather than merits.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,513 consumer bankruptcy cases from Pennsylvania's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7415n/an/a

Chapter 131,098n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Pro Se Works in Pennsylvania

The profile of a Pennsylvania pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the Pennsylvania median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in Pennsylvania

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The Pennsylvania exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

Pennsylvania Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the Pennsylvania exemption scheme:

Pennsylvania homestead: $0 (federal opt-in common) (federal $31,575/2025).

Pennsylvania auto exemption: federal $5,025 opt-in.

Pennsylvania wage protection: BANNED for consumer debts.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

## Pro Se Bankruptcy in Rhode Island [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/states/rhode-island.html

← prosebankruptcy.org home

Pro Se Bankruptcy in Rhode Island [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Rhode Island residents.

Yes, you can file bankruptcy without a lawyer (pro se) in Rhode Island. The federal bankruptcy courts in Rhode Island accept pro se filings, and the official forms are free at uscourts.gov. Pro se works best for a straightforward Chapter 7 with few assets and no disputes; it gets risky if you have property to protect, a business, income near the means-test limit, or any contested issue. Check Rhode Island's local rules and the court's self-help resources before filing, and confirm your exemptions, because mistakes on a pro se petition are hard to undo.

Pro Se Bankruptcy in Rhode Island - Overview

Individuals have the constitutional right to represent themselves under 28 U.S.C. Section 1654. Corporations and LLCs cannot file pro se - Rowland v. California Men's Colony, 506 U.S. 194 (1993). For individual Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 filers in Rhode Island, pro se is legally permitted but practically difficult.

Rhode Island Pro Se FactsValue

Chapter 7 pro se rate (FJC)n/a

Chapter 13 pro se rate (FJC)n/a

Bankruptcy districtsDistrict of Rhode Island

Local pro se ruleD.R.I. small docket; pro se paper filing.

Rhode Island Self-Help Resources

Rhode Island Legal Services.

Additional Rhode Island resources for pro se bankruptcy filers:

Law school bankruptcy clinics - where available (see above), these accept clinic-eligible clients.

U.S. Trustee Program - the UST does not represent debtors but will point out procedural problems; in Bankruptcy Administrator states (NC and SC) the Administrator handles this role.

Rhode Island Local Rule Pitfalls for Pro Se Filers

D.R.I. small docket; pro se paper filing.

Local form requirements. Rhode Island districts often have local cover sheets, pay-advice summaries, or tax-return cover forms that supplement the national Official Forms.

E-filing restrictions. Pro se filers generally cannot use CM/ECF unless they register and complete training. Paper filing is the default.

Paper originals for signatures. Many Rhode Island districts require wet-signed originals for petitions, schedules, and amendments.

Credit counseling certificate timing. The certificate must be dated before filing (no grace period except very narrow hardship exceptions).

341 meeting attendance requirements. In-person attendance rules vary by district; some Rhode Island courts require video, some allow telephone.

Redaction requirements under Rule 9037. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 9037 mandates SSN, account number, and minor-child redactions. Pro se filers are fully responsible for compliance.

See common pro se mistakes.

UPL (Unauthorized Practice of Law) in Rhode Island

RI Gen. Laws 11-27-2 UPL.

For pro se debtors, UPL has two practical faces:

Protection: Non-lawyers (friends, family, internet forum commenters) cannot give you legal advice in Rhode Island. If they do, their advice is unreliable and they may be prosecuted.

A BPP who crosses the line into legal advice commits UPL and can be sanctioned; the debtor may be allowed to recover fees paid. See 11 U.S.C. Section 110.

When Pro Se Works in Rhode Island

The profile of a Rhode Island pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the Rhode Island median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in Rhode Island

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The Rhode Island exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

Rhode Island Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the Rhode Island exemption scheme:

Rhode Island homestead: $500,000 (R.I.G.L. 9-26-4.1).

Rhode Island auto exemption: $12,000.

Rhode Island wage protection: 25%.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

## Pro Se Bankruptcy in Texas [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/states/texas.html

← prosebankruptcy.org home

Pro Se Bankruptcy in Texas [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Texas residents.

Yes, you can file bankruptcy without a lawyer (pro se) in Texas. The federal bankruptcy courts in Texas accept pro se filings, and the official forms are free at uscourts.gov. Pro se works best for a straightforward Chapter 7 with few assets and no disputes; it gets risky if you have property to protect, a business, income near the means-test limit, or any contested issue. Check Texas's local rules and the court's self-help resources before filing, and confirm your exemptions, because mistakes on a pro se petition are hard to undo.

Pro Se Bankruptcy in Texas - Overview

Individuals have the constitutional right to represent themselves under 28 U.S.C. Section 1654. Corporations and LLCs cannot file pro se - Rowland v. California Men's Colony, 506 U.S. 194 (1993). For individual Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 filers in Texas, pro se is legally permitted but practically difficult.

Texas Pro Se FactsValue

Chapter 7 pro se rate (FJC)100.0%

Chapter 13 pro se rate (FJC)100.0%

Bankruptcy districtsNorthern, Eastern, Southern, Western Districts (4)

Local pro se rule4 districts; TXSB (Houston) has especially robust pro se help desk.

Texas Self-Help Resources

Texas Legal Services Center; Lone Star Legal Aid.

Additional Texas resources for pro se bankruptcy filers:

LawHelp.org TX - triage tool linking to free/low-cost legal aid.

State bar lawyer referral service - 30-minute consultations often at reduced fee.

Court-run pro se clinics - many Texas bankruptcy judges host periodic free clinics; check the district's website.

Law school bankruptcy clinics - where available (see above), these accept clinic-eligible clients.

U.S. Trustee Program - the UST does not represent debtors but will point out procedural problems; in Bankruptcy Administrator states (NC and SC) the Administrator handles this role.

Texas Local Rule Pitfalls for Pro Se Filers

4 districts; TXSB (Houston) has especially robust pro se help desk.

Beyond the federal Bankruptcy Code and Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, each Texas bankruptcy district has its own Local Rules and Standing Orders that are NOT negotiable. Common pro se traps:

Local form requirements. Texas districts often have local cover sheets, pay-advice summaries, or tax-return cover forms that supplement the national Official Forms.

E-filing restrictions. Pro se filers generally cannot use CM/ECF unless they register and complete training. Paper filing is the default.

Paper originals for signatures. Many Texas districts require wet-signed originals for petitions, schedules, and amendments.

Credit counseling certificate timing. The certificate must be dated before filing (no grace period except very narrow hardship exceptions).

341 meeting attendance requirements. In-person attendance rules vary by district; some Texas courts require video, some allow telephone.

Redaction requirements under Rule 9037. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 9037 mandates SSN, account number, and minor-child redactions. Pro se filers are fully responsible for compliance.

See common pro se mistakes.

UPL (Unauthorized Practice of Law) in Texas

Tex. Gov. Code 81.101 UPL.

For pro se debtors, UPL has two practical faces:

Protection: Non-lawyers (friends, family, internet forum commenters) cannot give you legal advice in Texas. If they do, their advice is unreliable and they may be prosecuted.

Limit on help: The only non-lawyer assistance permitted in bankruptcy is from Bankruptcy Petition Preparers (BPPs) under 11 U.S.C. Section 110. BPPs may type the forms you tell them to type but may not advise on law. They must disclose their identity and fees.

A BPP who crosses the line into legal advice commits UPL and can be sanctioned; the debtor may be allowed to recover fees paid. See 11 U.S.C. Section 110.

Texas Federal Bankruptcy Data

Texas pro se debtors face the same federal rules as represented filers but without a licensed advocate. Dismissal rates tend to run higher for pro se cases, often for procedural reasons (missed deadlines, incomplete schedules) rather than merits.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 30,781 consumer bankruptcy cases from Texas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711,84497.8%2.0%

Chapter 1318,93736.8%63.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Pro Se Works in Texas

The profile of a Texas pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the Texas median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in Texas

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The Texas exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

Texas Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the Texas exemption scheme:

Texas homestead: Unlimited (10 acres urban / 100-200 rural) (Tex. Prop. 41.001).

Texas auto exemption: Unlimited one vehicle/family member.

Texas wage protection: BANNED for consumer debts.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

Related Texas Resources

Pro se checklist

Common pro se mistakes

FAQ

Missouri walkthrough (detailed model)

Texas filing procedure

Texas exemption list

1328(f) discharge eligibility screener

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in Washington

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The Washington exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

Washington Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the Washington exemption scheme:

Washington homestead: County median home price (RCW 6.13.030 (2021 update)).

Washington auto exemption: $3,250 ($6,500 joint).

Washington wage protection: 25% / 35x state MW.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

## Pro Se Bankruptcy in West Virginia [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/states/west-virginia.html

← prosebankruptcy.org home

Pro Se Bankruptcy in West Virginia [2026]: FJC Data, Clinics, and Local Rules

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for West Virginia residents.

Yes, you can file bankruptcy without a lawyer (pro se) in West Virginia. The federal bankruptcy courts in West Virginia accept pro se filings, and the official forms are free at uscourts.gov. Pro se works best for a straightforward Chapter 7 with few assets and no disputes; it gets risky if you have property to protect, a business, income near the means-test limit, or any contested issue. Check West Virginia's local rules and the court's self-help resources before filing, and confirm your exemptions, because mistakes on a pro se petition are hard to undo.

Pro Se Bankruptcy in West Virginia - Overview

Individuals have the constitutional right to represent themselves under 28 U.S.C. Section 1654. Corporations and LLCs cannot file pro se - Rowland v. California Men's Colony, 506 U.S. 194 (1993). For individual Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 filers in West Virginia, pro se is legally permitted but practically difficult.

West Virginia Pro Se FactsValue

Chapter 7 pro se rate (FJC)100.0%

Chapter 13 pro se rate (FJC)n/a

Bankruptcy districtsNorthern and Southern Districts

Local pro se ruleWVSB/WVNB small docket; pro se paper filing.

West Virginia Self-Help Resources

Legal Aid of WV.

Additional West Virginia resources for pro se bankruptcy filers:

LawHelp.org WV - triage tool linking to free/low-cost legal aid.

State bar lawyer referral service - 30-minute consultations often at reduced fee.

Court-run pro se clinics - many West Virginia bankruptcy judges host periodic free clinics; check the district's website.

Law school bankruptcy clinics - where available (see above), these accept clinic-eligible clients.

U.S. Trustee Program - the UST does not represent debtors but will point out procedural problems; in Bankruptcy Administrator states (NC and SC) the Administrator handles this role.

West Virginia Local Rule Pitfalls for Pro Se Filers

WVSB/WVNB small docket; pro se paper filing.

Beyond the federal Bankruptcy Code and Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure, each West Virginia bankruptcy district has its own Local Rules and Standing Orders that are NOT negotiable. Common pro se traps:

Local form requirements. West Virginia districts often have local cover sheets, pay-advice summaries, or tax-return cover forms that supplement the national Official Forms.

E-filing restrictions. Pro se filers generally cannot use CM/ECF unless they register and complete training. Paper filing is the default.

Paper originals for signatures. Many West Virginia districts require wet-signed originals for petitions, schedules, and amendments.

Credit counseling certificate timing. The certificate must be dated before filing (no grace period except very narrow hardship exceptions).

341 meeting attendance requirements. In-person attendance rules vary by district; some West Virginia courts require video, some allow telephone.

Redaction requirements under Rule 9037. Federal Rule of Bankruptcy Procedure 9037 mandates SSN, account number, and minor-child redactions. Pro se filers are fully responsible for compliance.

See common pro se mistakes.

UPL (Unauthorized Practice of Law) in West Virginia

W. Va. Code 30-2-5 UPL.

For pro se debtors, UPL has two practical faces:

Protection: Non-lawyers (friends, family, internet forum commenters) cannot give you legal advice in West Virginia. If they do, their advice is unreliable and they may be prosecuted.

Limit on help: The only non-lawyer assistance permitted in bankruptcy is from Bankruptcy Petition Preparers (BPPs) under 11 U.S.C. Section 110. BPPs may type the forms you tell them to type but may not advise on law. They must disclose their identity and fees.

A BPP who crosses the line into legal advice commits UPL and can be sanctioned; the debtor may be allowed to recover fees paid. See 11 U.S.C. Section 110.

West Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

West Virginia pro se debtors face the same federal rules as represented filers but without a licensed advocate. Dismissal rates tend to run higher for pro se cases, often for procedural reasons (missed deadlines, incomplete schedules) rather than merits.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 60 consumer bankruptcy cases from West Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 75498.1%1.9%

Chapter 136n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Pro Se Works in West Virginia

The profile of a West Virginia pro se case most likely to reach discharge:

Chapter 7 no-asset case. Income below the West Virginia median, no non-exempt assets, no contested claims.

Clean financial record. No recent credit transactions, no transferred property, no co-signed debts in dispute.

Single-debtor unsecured profile. Credit cards, medical bills, unsecured personal loans. No secured claim disputes.

Complete and accurate schedules. Every creditor listed, every asset listed, every income source listed.

Documentation discipline. You keep copies of everything, read every court notice, respond to every trustee request within deadlines.

No litigation. No pending lawsuits, no adversary-proceeding targets (preference claims, non-dischargeability).

When Pro Se Fails in West Virginia

Cases that go wrong tend to share these features:

Chapter 13. Plan drafting requires specialized knowledge of disposable income calculation, good-faith tests, and trustee practice. Pro se Chapter 13 dismissal rates run substantially higher than attorney-filed.

Chapter 11 / Subchapter V / business entity. Corporate debtors cannot proceed pro se. Attempting to do so results in dismissal.

Contested homestead exemption. The West Virginia exemption scheme can be complex (see homestead overview below).

Student loans, tax debts, or non-dischargeability questions. Adversary proceedings usually require counsel.

Concurrent divorce, criminal, or tax matter. Cross-proceeding coordination is hard pro se.

Missed deadlines. The #1 procedural dismissal driver.

West Virginia Homestead and Exemption Context

A critical pro se consideration is the West Virginia exemption scheme:

West Virginia homestead: $35,000 (W. Va. Code 38-10-4).

West Virginia auto exemption: $7,500.

West Virginia wage protection: 20%.

Pro se debtors must affirmatively claim exemptions on Schedule C. Exemptions not listed are waived. Errors here can cost your home, car, or wages.

## Additional FAQ Pages


### Can I file bankruptcy without a lawyer? - Pro Se Bankruptcy Guide
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/paa/can-i-file-bankruptcy-without-a-lawyer.html

Skip to content

prosebankruptcy.org

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › Can I file bankruptcy without a lawyer?

People Also Ask

Can I file bankruptcy without a lawyer?

Yes, you have a constitutional right to file bankruptcy without a lawyer (pro se). About 8-10% of Chapter 7 cases are filed pro se. Success rates are lower than attorney-filed cases but still substantial. Pro se filing works best for straightforward Chapter 7 cases with primarily unsecured debt and minimal assets.

Filing bankruptcy without an attorney is legal and, for many people with straightforward cases, entirely achievable.

When Pro Se Works Well

Simple Chapter 7: Primarily unsecured debt (credit cards, medical bills), below-median income, few assets, no recent property transfers

No real estate: Cases involving homes, mortgages, and homestead exemptions add significant complexity

No business: Self-employment income and business debts complicate the means test and schedules

No prior filings: Repeat filings involve timing rules and strategic considerations

The Process

Complete the pre-filing credit counseling course (approximately $15-25 online)

Fill out the official bankruptcy forms (about 50-70 pages total for Chapter 7)

File the petition, schedules, and statements with the bankruptcy court clerk

Pay the $338 filing fee (or apply for a fee waiver or installment payments)

Attend the 341 meeting of creditors (about 30 days after filing)

Complete the financial management course (post-filing, approximately $15-25)

Receive your discharge (about 60 days after the 341 meeting)

Pro Se Success Rates

Pro se filers have a lower discharge rate than attorney-represented filers, primarily because of filing errors, incomplete schedules, and missed deadlines. However, careful preparation and attention to detail can overcome these challenges. The court clerk's office can answer procedural questions (though not legal questions), and many courts offer pro se clinics.

### How much does it cost to file bankruptcy yourself? - Pro Se Bankruptcy Guide
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/paa/how-much-does-it-cost-to-file-bankruptcy-yourself.html

Skip to content

prosebankruptcy.org

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › How much does it cost to file bankruptcy yourself?

People Also Ask

How much does it cost to file bankruptcy yourself?

Filing Chapter 7 bankruptcy yourself costs $338 for the court filing fee plus $30-50 for the two required credit counseling courses, for a total of approximately $370-390. Low-income filers can apply for a fee waiver, potentially reducing the cost to just the counseling courses. This compares to $1,400-$2,900 total when hiring an attorney.

The cost savings of filing pro se are significant, but you should weigh them against the risks.

Pro Se Cost Breakdown

Court filing fee: $338 for Chapter 7, $313 for Chapter 13

Pre-filing credit counseling: $10-25 (many approved agencies offer online courses)

Post-filing financial management course: $10-25

Total: Approximately $360-390

Fee Waivers

If your household income is below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, you can apply to have the filing fee waived entirely. The court uses Form 103B for this request. Approval is common for filers at or near the poverty level. If you do not qualify for a full waiver, you can request installment payments over 120 days.

Hidden Costs to Consider

Document preparation time: Expect 20-40 hours to properly complete all forms

Potential errors: Mistakes can lead to case dismissal, which wastes the filing fee and delays relief

Lost exemptions: Failure to properly claim exemptions could result in losing property you could have kept

When the Savings Are Not Worth It

If your case involves a home, a business, non-exempt assets, or any complexity beyond basic unsecured debt, the cost of an attorney is likely a wise investment. Many bankruptcy attorneys offer payment plans, and the protection they provide often exceeds their fee.

### Common Questions - Pro Se Bankruptcy Guide
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/paa/index.html

prosebankruptcy.org

Home
Questions

Common Questions

Clear, data-backed answers to the most frequently asked questions

Can I file bankruptcy without a lawyer?

How much does it cost to file bankruptcy yourself?

What forms do I need to file bankruptcy pro se?

Filing Bankruptcy Pro Se: What You Need to Know

The decision to file bankruptcy without an attorney should be made carefully. While it is your legal right, bankruptcy involves complex rules about exemptions, means testing, reaffirmation agreements, and discharge eligibility that can significantly affect the outcome of your case. Courts provide standardized forms but limited guidance on strategy. If you proceed pro se, take advantage of every free resource available: court self-help desks, law school bankruptcy clinics, legal aid organizations, and the detailed instructions accompanying each official form.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I file bankruptcy without a lawyer?

Yes, you have the constitutional right to file bankruptcy pro se (without an attorney). However, bankruptcy law is complex and errors can result in dismissal, loss of property, or failure to discharge debts. Many courts offer self-help resources, and legal aid organizations may provide free or low-cost assistance.

What are the risks of filing pro se?

Common risks include incorrectly valuing assets, failing to claim all available exemptions, missing deadlines, improperly listing creditors, and making errors on the means test. These mistakes can lead to case dismissal, loss of exempt property, or non-dischargeable debts that could have been discharged with proper counsel.

Where can I get help filing bankruptcy pro se?

Free resources include the court's self-help desk, bankruptcy clinic programs at law schools, legal aid societies, and the court's local rules and forms. The U.S. Courts website (uscourts.gov) provides official forms and instructions. Some nonprofit organizations also offer free bankruptcy preparation assistance.

### What forms do I need to file bankruptcy pro se? - Pro Se Bankruptcy Guide
Source: https://prosebankruptcy.org/paa/what-forms-do-i-need-to-file-bankruptcy-pro-se.html

Skip to content

prosebankruptcy.org

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › What forms do I need to file bankruptcy pro se?

People Also Ask

What forms do I need to file bankruptcy pro se?

For Chapter 7, you need approximately 23 official forms including the Voluntary Petition (Form 101), Schedules A/B through J (assets, liabilities, income, expenses), Statement of Financial Affairs (Form 107), means test forms (122A-1 or 122A-2), and the credit counseling certificate. All forms are free from the U.S. Courts website.

The official bankruptcy forms are standardized nationwide and available for free download. Here is what you need.

Core Chapter 7 Forms

Form 101: Voluntary Petition - basic case information, filing type, debtor details

Form 101A/B: Additional information (if applicable)

Schedule A/B: All property you own (real estate, personal property, financial assets)

Schedule C: Exemptions you are claiming

Schedule D: Secured debts (mortgage, car loans)

Schedule E/F: Unsecured debts (priority and general)

Schedule G: Executory contracts and unexpired leases

Schedule H: Co-debtors

Schedule I: Current income

Schedule J: Current expenses

Form 106Dec: Declaration about schedules

Form 107: Statement of Financial Affairs - 28 questions about your financial history

Form 108: Statement of Intention (what you will do with secured property)

Form 119: Bankruptcy Petition Preparer declaration (if someone helped prepare forms)

Form 121: Social Security number statement (filed separately, not public)

Form 122A-1: Means test - Chapter 7 (below median)

Form 122A-2: Means test - Chapter 7 (above median, if applicable)

Where to Get the Forms

All official forms are available free at uscourts.gov/forms/bankruptcy-forms. Many courts also provide local forms and instructions specific to their district. Check your court's website for any local requirements.

Take your time completing these forms. Accuracy matters more than speed. Every item on your schedules is signed under penalty of perjury.
